chart.legend.any: any channel is fine, low risk (green)
chart.legend.trusted: trusted channel only, call or in person (red)
guide.title: How an rsatoy exchange works
guide.step.1: 1. Recipient: run rsatoy init to make a key pair. Nothing is sent.
guide.step.2: 2. Recipient: send the public key to the sender by email or chat. Anyone may see it.
guide.step.3: 3. On a call or in person, the recipient reads the fingerprint aloud. The sender runs rsatoy encrypt and only goes on if it matches.
guide.step.4: 4. Sender: type the secret, then send the message block by email or chat. Keep the message ID on screen.
guide.step.5: 5. Recipient: run rsatoy decrypt and read the message ID to the sender on a call. Only go on if it matches.
guide.step.6: 6. Recipient: enter the passphrase. The secret is copied to the clipboard.
guide.tip: Tip: run rsatoy with no arguments to be walked through each step.
g.welcome: rsatoy will walk you through sharing a secret safely, one step at a time.
g.role: Are you receiving a secret or sending one? Type r to receive or s to send:
g.r1.what: You will make your key pair. The private key stays on this computer, locked with a passphrase you choose.
g.r1.exists: You already have a key pair, so this step is skipped.
g.r2.what: Send your public key to the sender by email or chat. It is not secret, so any channel is fine.
g.r3.what: Call the sender, or meet in person, and read this fingerprint aloud. They will check it matches what they see.
g.r4.what: Wait for the sender to send you a message block by email or chat.
g.r5.what: Paste the message block below. rsatoy will show its message ID, which you will read to the sender on a call.
g.r6.what: Enter your passphrase to decrypt the message.
g.r6.done: Done. Paste the secret where you need it.
g.s2.what: The recipient will send you their public key by email or chat. Paste it below, or type the path of a file that holds it.
g.s2.paste: Paste the public key block or a file path, then press Enter:
g.s3.what: Call the recipient, or meet in person, and ask them to read their fingerprint aloud.
g.s4.what: Type the secret. It will not show on screen.
g.s4.send: Send this message block to the recipient by email or chat:
g.s4.keep: Keep this window open: the recipient will read this ID back to you in step 5.
g.s5.what: The recipient will read you a message ID on the call. Check it is the same as this one: %s
g.s5.mismatch: It does not match. Someone may have swapped the message. Tell the recipient not to use it, and start again.
g.s6.what: Done. The recipient can now decrypt the secret.
